commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug

commands.name: code-review

commands.name: simplify

commands.name: doctor

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	There is no AGENTS.md in this repository.
4	
5	## Project context
6	
7	- **Engine:** Godot 4.7.2 stable. `godot/project.godot` declares `config/features=PackedStringArray("4.7", "GL Compatibility")`; every log in `logs/*.log` starts with `Godot Engine v4.7.2.stable.official`.
8	- **Renderer:** GL Compatibility. `godot/project.godot` `[rendering]` sets `renderer/rendering_method="gl_compatibility"` and `renderer/rendering_method.mobile="gl_compatibility"`. No `rendering/viewport/hdr_2d` key is present, so 2D blending is on sRGB values (as CHANGE-BRIEF.md A4 assumes).
9	- **Viewport:** 640 × 360, window override 1280 × 720, stretch mode `canvas_items` (`godot/project.godot` `[display]`). One texel of a sprite drawn at scale 0.5 is one window pixel.
10	- **Main scene:** `res://game/main.tscn` (`godot/project.godot` `run/main_scene`). `godot/game/main.tscn` is a single `Node2D` named `WalkerJumpman` with `res://game/session.gd` attached; everything else is built in code.
11	- **Game state that drives the effect:** `godot/game/session.gd`. In `_physics_process` it sets `water_ticks = EXTINGUISH_TICKS + 60` on a W press in range of the blocking fire, counts it down, and writes `player.hosing = water_ticks > 0` every physics tick. `EXTINGUISH_TICKS := 240`. `restart_attempt()` resets `water_ticks = 0`; it is called by `start_session()`, by the R key handler in `_unhandled_input`, and by the DYING timeout in `_physics_process`. The driver reads `player.hosing` only; nothing in `session.gd` changes.
12	- **How the shaded object is drawn:** `godot/features/player/player.gd` builds, in `_ready()`, a holder `Node2D` `art` (`show_behind_parent = true`) and inside it one `Sprite2D` `sprite` with `centered = false`. `show_pose()` swaps `sprite.texture` to `res://art/character/<pose>.png`, sets `sprite.position` to minus the anchor from `godot/art/character/anchors.json`, and sets `art.scale = Vector2(0.5 * facing, 0.5)`. `_update_pose()` picks the `hose` pose when `hosing` is true and he is grounded and still. The `hose` anchor is `[58.8, 84.0]`; `hose.png` is 126 × 84 texels. The rescue bag and survivor heads are code-drawn in `player.gd` `_draw()` on the `CharacterBody2D` itself, not on `sprite`. There is no player `.tscn`; the player is `Player.new()` in `session.gd` `_ready()`.
13	- **Hose pose texture import:** `godot/art/character/hose.png.import` has `compress/mode=0` (Lossless) and `mipmaps/generate=false`.
14	- **3D object for the textured shader:** node `Hydrant` in `godot/scenes3d/props_room.tscn`, instancing `res://props3d/hydrant.glb` at x = −0.8. The scene also holds `WorldEnvironment` (flat background, ambient energy 0.6), `Sun` (`DirectionalLight3D`, shadows on), `Camera3D`, `RescueBag` at x = 0, `Flame` at x = 0.8, and a 1.8 m reference pole at x = 1.5.
15	- **Where the hydrant's material comes from today:** embedded in the glb. `godot/props3d/hydrant.glb` carries two glTF materials, `hydrant_red` (baseColorFactor ≈ 0.527, 0.041, 0.024) and `hydrant_grey`, both created as flat colours by `flat_material()` in `tools/blender/build_hydrant.py`. The mesh has `TEXCOORD_0`. `godot/props3d/hydrant.glb.import` has `materials/extract=0`, `_subresources={}` and `meshes/ensure_tangents=true`: no external material or per-material override exists yet, so the "Use External" path in CHANGE-BRIEF.md C1 is still to be set up in the editor.
16	- **Existing tests (`godot/tests/`), all `extends SceneTree`:** `test_game.gd` (41 checks; also writes `evidence/mechanics-*.json`), `test_keyboard.gd` (14 checks, synthetic `InputEventKey`), `test_audio.gd` (14 checks), `check_props.gd` (A3 prop geometry; prints `RESULT: PASS`). Tests drive hosing through `game.player.test_water_pressed = true` with `test_control = true` (`test_game.gd`). **Not tests:** `route_driver.gd` (scripted route helper), `capture_game.gd` and `capture_props.gd` (screenshot scripts, need a window), `run_check_props.sh` (A3 runner, superseded by `scripts/run-test.sh` for A5).
17	- **Test runner:** `scripts/run-test.sh <test-file.gd> <fps>` runs `godot --headless --path godot --script res://tests/<file> --fixed-fps <fps>` under `timeout 120`, tees to `logs/<name>_<fps>fps.log`, and exits 1 on any `SHADER ERROR` or `SCRIPT ERROR` line (exit 124 = hung). `GODOT` may name the binary; it falls back to `~/Downloads/Godot.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot` (adapt this path on another machine). It forwards no extra user args, so `check_props.gd`'s `-- mutate` mode is not reachable through it.
18	- **Exact test commands (from the repository root):**
19	
20	  ```
21	  scripts/run-test.sh test_game.gd 60
22	  scripts/run-test.sh test_keyboard.gd 60
23	  scripts/run-test.sh test_audio.gd 60
24	  scripts/run-test.sh check_props.gd 60
25	  ```
26	
27	  Baseline on commit `025acf1` (logs in `logs/`): `test_game` 41/41, `test_keyboard` 14/14, `check_props` `RESULT: PASS`, `test_audio` 12/14. The two `test_audio` failures (`music-behaviour`, `music-loops`) occur only under `--fixed-fps` (14/14 without it) and are pre-existing; they are not caused by this change and must not be "fixed" as part of it. New A5 tests run the same way at 30, 60 and 144 fps.
28	
29	## Headless facts
30	
31	What a `scripts/run-test.sh` run on this machine can and cannot observe:
32	
33	- Headless Godot uses a dummy renderer: nothing is drawn, no viewport image exists, no pixel can be read. Every claim about the look (colour, glow strength, roughness, bumps, the hint-experiment bands) is a human check in the editor, recorded in `a5/TEST-REPORT.md`.
34	- `Shader.get_shader_uniform_list()` works headlessly and returns names and types; it returns an empty list for a shader that failed to parse. Uniform defaults are not reported headlessly; read them from the `.gdshader` source text.
35	- `ShaderMaterial.set_shader_parameter()` stores any name and any value without error, and `get_shader_parameter()` reads it back, so a set-then-get round trip proves nothing about the shader. Only the uniform-list assertion catches a renamed or missing uniform.
36	- `--fixed-fps N` pins the physics and process step to 1/N s of game time; a run does not take real time. A ramp written in `delta` seconds must take the same number of game-seconds at 30, 60 and 144.
37	- Real input works headlessly: `Input.action_press()` / `action_release()`, and the player's `test_water_pressed` hook used by `test_game.gd`. The hosing state can be driven through the real game loop.
38	- Audio timing is not headless-safe under `--fixed-fps`: `AudioStreamPlayer` playback position runs on the audio clock, which is why `test_audio.gd` loses two checks when pinned.
39	- A `.import` file is written by the editor's importer; `godot --headless --path godot --import` reproduces it from the source file and the `[params]` block, and `ConfigFile` can read it in a test.
40	
41	## Current change
42	
43	@CHANGE-BRIEF.md
44	
45	## Ownership
46	
47	Files in `godot/shaders/` are hand-written by the human and are never edited by an agent. That covers `hose_glow.gdshader`, `hint_experiment.gdshader` and `hydrant_surface.gdshader` named in the brief. An agent may read them, write drivers, tests and scenes that use them, and report what it observes; it does not create, edit, rename or delete anything under `godot/shaders/`.
48	
49	## Out of scope
50	
51	This change adds presentation that reads game state. It must not:
52	
53	- Edit `godot/game/session.gd` game logic: the hose state machine, `EXTINGUISH_TICKS`, the +60 water linger, `FIRE_DEATH_HOLD`, death, rescue, timer, pause, audio or input handling. Any A5 driver reads `player.hosing` and writes only a shader parameter.
54	- Change collision, movement, input mapping or tuning (`godot/features/player/player.gd` physics, `tuning.gd`, `godot/levels/first_steps.json`).
55	- Alter the existing tests or their expectations (`test_game.gd`, `test_keyboard.gd`, `test_audio.gd`, `check_props.gd`), including the pre-existing `test_audio` fixed-fps failures.
56	- Touch the HUD (`godot/ui/hud.gd`), the fires, the survivors, the background or the generated art under `godot/art/character/` and `godot/art/env/`.
57	- Put the glow material anywhere but `player.sprite`. The code-drawn rescue bag and survivor heads must stay their own colours.
58	- Change the hydrant mesh, `hydrant.glb`, or the other props and their placement; the second hydrant is a new instance at x = −1.6, the existing one stays at x = −0.8. Lighting and the environment in `props_room.tscn` stay as they are.
59	- Edit `project.godot` rendering settings (no `hdr_2d`, no renderer switch).
60	- Rewrite the v1 text of `CHANGE-BRIEF.md`; new findings go under its Revisions heading with a date.
61	- Write or edit any `.gdshader` (see Ownership). Edit `scripts/run-test.sh`.
62	
63	## Unconfirmed
64	
65	- CHANGE-BRIEF.md Part B names `godot/tests/write_grey_strip.gd`; it is planned, not yet written. `godot/art/hint/`, `godot/art/textures/`, `godot/shaders/` and `godot/materials/` do not exist yet.
66	- The Poly Haven `rusty_metal_sheet` files, their licence and the `ATTRIBUTION.md` are described in the brief only; nothing is downloaded.
67	- The pixel values for P1–P3 come from a headless `Image.load_from_file` probe of `hose.png` (not committed); the sky texel from the same probe of `env_bg.png`. They are not editor measurements.
68	- Whether `hint_range` clamps `set_shader_parameter` values, and how GL Compatibility treats `source_color` in 2D and the Part B quads, are predictions in the brief, not facts established from this repository.
69	- Whether `--fixed-fps 30` and `144` runs pass the existing tests: only 60 fps logs exist in `logs/`.

- **Game state that drives the effect:** `godot/game/session.gd`. In `_physics_process` it sets `water_ticks = EXTINGUISH_TICKS + 60` on a W press in range of the blocking fire, counts it down, and writes `player.hosing = water_ticks > 0` every physics tick. `EXTINGUISH_TICKS := 240`. `restart_attempt()` resets `water_ticks = 0`; it is called by `start_session()`, by the R key handler in `_unhandled_input`, and by the DYING timeout in `_physics_process`. The driver reads `player.hosing` only; nothing in `session.gd` changes.
- **How the shaded object is drawn:** `godot/features/player/player.gd` builds, in `_ready()`, a holder `Node2D` `art` (`show_behind_parent = true`) and inside it one `Sprite2D` `sprite` with `centered = false`. `show_pose()` swaps `sprite.texture` to `res://art/character/<pose>.png`, sets `sprite.position` to minus the anchor from `godot/art/character/anchors.json`, and sets `art.scale = Vector2(0.5 * facing, 0.5)`. `_update_pose()` picks the `hose` pose when `hosing` is true and he is grounded and still. The `hose` anchor is `[58.8, 84.0]`; `hose.png` is 126 × 84 texels. The rescue bag and survivor heads are code-drawn in `player.gd` `_draw()` on the `CharacterBody2D` itself, not on `sprite`. There is no player `.tscn`; the player is `Player.new()` in `session.gd` `_ready()`.
- **Hose pose texture import:** `godot/art/character/hose.png.import` has `compress/mode=0` (Lossless) and `mipmaps/generate=false`.
- **3D object for the textured shader:** node `Hydrant` in `godot/scenes3d/props_room.tscn`, instancing `res://props3d/hydrant.glb` at x = −0.8. The scene also holds `WorldEnvironment` (flat background, ambient energy 0.6), `Sun` (`DirectionalLight3D`, shadows on), `Camera3D`, `RescueBag` at x = 0, `Flame` at x = 0.8, and a 1.8 m reference pole at x = 1.5.
- **Where the hydrant's material comes from today:** embedded in the glb. `godot/props3d/hydrant.glb` carries two glTF materials, `hydrant_red` (baseColorFactor ≈ 0.527, 0.041, 0.024) and `hydrant_grey`, both created as flat colours by `flat_material()` in `tools/blender/build_hydrant.py`. The mesh has `TEXCOORD_0`. `godot/props3d/hydrant.glb.import` has `materials/extract=0`, `_subresources={}` and `meshes/ensure_tangents=true`: no external material or per-material override exists yet, so the "Use External" path in CHANGE-BRIEF.md C1 is still to be set up in the editor.
- **Existing tests (`godot/tests/`), all `extends SceneTree`:** `test_game.gd` (41 checks; also writes `evidence/mechanics-*.json`), `test_keyboard.gd` (14 checks, synthetic `InputEventKey`), `test_audio.gd` (14 checks), `check_props.gd` (A3 prop geometry; prints `RESULT: PASS`). Tests drive hosing through `game.player.test_water_pressed = true` with `test_control = true` (`test_game.gd`). **Not tests:** `route_driver.gd` (scripted route helper), `capture_game.gd` and `capture_props.gd` (screenshot scripts, need a window), `run_check_props.sh` (A3 runner, superseded by `scripts/run-test.sh` for A5).
- **Test runner:** `scripts/run-test.sh <test-file.gd> <fps>` runs `godot --headless --path godot --script res://tests/<file> --fixed-fps <fps>` under `timeout 120`, tees to `logs/<name>_<fps>fps.log`, and exits 1 on any `SHADER ERROR` or `SCRIPT ERROR` line (exit 124 = hung). `GODOT` may name the binary; it falls back to `~/Downloads/Godot.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot` (adapt this path on another machine). It forwards no extra user args, so `check_props.gd`'s `-- mutate` mode is not reachable through it.
- **Exact test commands (from the repository root):**

  ```
  scripts/run-test.sh test_game.gd 60
  scripts/run-test.sh test_keyboard.gd 60
  scripts/run-test.sh test_audio.gd 60
  scripts/run-test.sh check_props.gd 60
  ```

  Baseline on commit `025acf1` (logs in `logs/`): `test_game` 41/41, `test_keyboard` 14/14, `check_props` `RESULT: PASS`, `test_audio` 12/14. The two `test_audio` failures (`music-behaviour`, `music-loops`) occur only under `--fixed-fps` (14/14 without it) and are pre-existing; they are not caused by this change and must not be "fixed" as part of it. New A5 tests run the same way at 30, 60 and 144 fps.

## Headless facts

What a `scripts/run-test.sh` run on this machine can and cannot observe:

- Headless Godot uses a dummy renderer: nothing is drawn, no viewport image exists, no pixel can be read. Every claim about the look (colour, glow strength, roughness, bumps, the hint-experiment bands) is a human check in the editor, recorded in `a5/TEST-REPORT.md`.
- `Shader.get_shader_uniform_list()` works headlessly and returns names and types; it returns an empty list for a shader that failed to parse. Uniform defaults are not reported headlessly; read them from the `.gdshader` source text.
- `ShaderMaterial.set_shader_parameter()` stores any name and any value without error, and `get_shader_parameter()` reads it back, so a set-then-get round trip proves nothing about the shader. Only the uniform-list assertion catches a renamed or missing uniform.
- `--fixed-fps N` pins the physics and process step to 1/N s of game time; a run does not take real time. A ramp written in `delta` seconds must take the same number of game-seconds at 30, 60 and 144.
- Real input works headlessly: `Input.action_press()` / `action_release()`, and the player's `test_water_pressed` hook used by `test_game.gd`. The hosing state can be driven through the real game loop.
- Audio timing is not headless-safe under `--fixed-fps`: `AudioStreamPlayer` playback position runs on the audio clock, which is why `test_audio.gd` loses two checks when pinned.
- A `.import` file is written by the editor's importer; `godot --headless --path godot --import` reproduces it from the source file and the `[params]` block, and `ConfigFile` can read it in a test.

## Current change

@CHANGE-BRIEF.md

## Ownership

Files in `godot/shaders/` are hand-written by the human and are never edited by an agent. That covers `hose_glow.gdshader`, `hint_experiment.gdshader` and `hydrant_surface.gdshader` named in the brief. An agent may read them, write drivers, tests and scenes that use them, and report what it observes; it does not create, edit, rename or delete anything under `godot/shaders/`.

## Out of scope

This change adds presentation that reads game state. It must not:

- Edit `godot/game/session.gd` game logic: the hose state machine, `EXTINGUISH_TICKS`, the +60 water linger, `FIRE_DEATH_HOLD`, death, rescue, timer, pause, audio or input handling. Any A5 driver reads `player.hosing` and writes only a shader parameter.
- Change collision, movement, input mapping or tuning (`godot/features/player/player.gd` physics, `tuning.gd`, `godot/levels/first_steps.json`).
- Alter the existing tests or their expectations (`test_game.gd`, `test_keyboard.gd`, `test_audio.gd`, `check_props.gd`), including the pre-existing `test_audio` fixed-fps failures.
- Touch the HUD (`godot/ui/hud.gd`), the fires, the survivors, the background or the generated art under `godot/art/character/` and `godot/art/env/`.
- Put the glow material anywhere but `player.sprite`. The code-drawn rescue bag and survivor heads must stay their own colours.
- Change the hydrant mesh, `hydrant.glb`, or the other props and their placement; the second hydrant is a new instance at x = −1.6, the existing one stays at x = −0.8. Lighting and the environment in `props_room.tscn` stay as they are.
- Edit `project.godot` rendering settings (no `hdr_2d`, no renderer switch).
- Rewrite the v1 text of `CHANGE-BRIEF.md`; new findings go under its Revisions heading with a date.
- Write or edit any `.gdshader` (see Ownership). Edit `scripts/run-test.sh`.

## Unconfirmed

- CHANGE-BRIEF.md Part B names `godot/tests/write_grey_strip.gd`; it is planned, not yet written. `godot/art/hint/`, `godot/art/textures/`, `godot/shaders/` and `godot/materials/` do not exist yet.
- The Poly Haven `rusty_metal_sheet` files, their licence and the `ATTRIBUTION.md` are described in the brief only; nothing is downloaded.
- The pixel values for P1–P3 come from a headless `Image.load_from_file` probe of `hose.png` (not committed); the sky texel from the same probe of `env_bg.png`. They are not editor measurements.
- Whether `hint_range` clamps `set_shader_parameter` values, and how GL Compatibility treats `source_color` in 2D and the Part B quads, are predictions in the brief, not facts established from this repository.
- Whether `--fixed-fps 30` and `144` runs pass the existing tests: only 60 fps logs exist in `logs/`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/run-test.sh <test-file.gd> <fps|realtime> [timeout-seconds]
set -o pipefail
mkdir -p logs
if [ "$2" = "realtime" ]; then
    fps_args=(); tag="realtime"
else
    fps_args=(--fixed-fps "$2"); tag="${2}fps"
fi
log="logs/$(basename "$1" .gd)_${tag}.log"
timeout "${3:-120}" godot --headless "${fps_args[@]}" --path godot --script "res://tests/$1" 2>&1 | tee "$log"
status=$?
if grep -qE "SHADER ERROR|SCRIPT ERROR" "$log"; then status=1; fi
exit $status

content.content:
1	# walker-ninja-firefighter-joe
2	
3	My CSYE 7270 game, built up one assignment at a time. Each assignment is a git tag: **`a2`** (generated art, sound and music; submitted from the class repo at commit `50a1797`), **`a3`** (three simple 3D props), **`a5`** (two hand-written shaders, their materials, and the Godot shading language).
4	
5	## Assignment 5 — shaders, materials, and the Godot shading language
6	
7	Two shaders I typed by hand, and the materials that use them. **Extinguisho glows pale blue while he hoses** (a `canvas_item` shader on his sprite, driven from the game's `player.hosing` state by a small script Claude Code wrote), and the **A3 hydrant gets a real surface** (a `spatial` shader that reads Poly Haven's rusty-metal colour, roughness and normal maps, with two materials: freshly painted and rusty). A third small shader is the **hint experiment** (one grey strip sampled as colour and as data), and a fourth is Godot's own, generated from a StandardMaterial3D, which I read and annotated.
8	
9	**Docs:** [CHANGE-BRIEF](CHANGE-BRIEF.md) (v1 committed before any shader or prompt; Revisions 1–4) · [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) (agent draft, then my review) · [`a5/`](a5/): [TEST-REPORT](a5/TEST-REPORT.md) · [LANGUAGE-NOTES](a5/LANGUAGE-NOTES.md) · [STANDARD-GENERATED-ANNOTATED](a5/STANDARD-GENERATED-ANNOTATED.md) · [FRICTIONAL](a5/FRICTIONAL.md) · [SOURCES](a5/SOURCES.md) · evidence (captures, mutation logs, playtest screenshots) in `a5/evidence/`, prompts in `a5/prompts/`, `claude -p` transcripts in `a5/sessions/` · [`godot/MATERIALS.md`](godot/MATERIALS.md) (the audit) · texture credits in [`godot/art/textures/rusty_metal_sheet/ATTRIBUTION.md`](godot/art/textures/rusty_metal_sheet/ATTRIBUTION.md).
10	
11	**Versions:** Godot 4.7.2 stable, GL Compatibility renderer · macOS 26.6.2 (Apple M1) · Claude Code 2.1.285 (`claude-fable-5-1`) for the driver, tests, audit and film.
12	
13	### What this assignment added
14	
15	| Path | What |
16	|---|---|
17	| `godot/shaders/hose_glow.gdshader` | **mine**, 8 lines: `glow` (float, `hint_range`) and `glow_color` (`source_color`); the colour line `COLOR.rgb = mix(COLOR.rgb, glow_color.rgb, glow);` |
18	| `godot/features/player/hose_glow.gd` (+ 2-line hook in `player.gd`) | the driver (agent): one `ShaderMaterial` on the sprite; `glow` ramps 0 → band in 0.25 s, breathes 0.4–0.8 at 1 s while hosing, ramps to 0 in 0.25 s after; scaled `delta`, never writes game state |
19	| `godot/shaders/hydrant_surface.gdshader` | **mine**, 25 lines: `albedo_tex : source_color`, `rough_tex : hint_default_white`, `normal_tex : hint_normal`; five dials in `paint` and `surface` groups |
20	| `godot/materials/hydrant_fresh.tres`, `hydrant_rusty.tres` | two materials, one shader: rust 0.1 / roughness 0.7 vs 0.9 / 1.4; fresh bound through the glb importer's Use External, rusty as a surface override on a second hydrant in `props_room.tscn` |
21	| `godot/art/textures/rusty_metal_sheet/` | Poly Haven *Rusty Metal Sheet* (Amal Kumar, CC0), `diff` / `rough` / `nor_gl` bound, `nor_dx` for calibration only; explicit `.import` settings; `ATTRIBUTION.md` |
22	| `godot/shaders/hint_experiment.gdshader`, `materials/hint_as_*.tres`, `scenes3d/hint_experiment.tscn`, `tests/write_grey_strip.gd`, `art/hint/grey_3x1.png` | **mine** (the shader): the hint experiment, Linear tonemap at exposure 1.0 |
23	| `godot/shaders/standard_generated.gdshader`, `scenes3d/scratch_standard.tscn` | Godot's generated shader from a converted StandardMaterial3D; nothing in the game uses it |
24	| `godot/tests/test_hose_glow.gd` | agent: 15 checks through real input events at 30 / 60 / 144 fps |
25	| `godot/tests/test_materials.gd`, `normal_map_check.gd`, `calibrate_normal_maps.gd` | agent audit test (35 checks), the assignment's curl check, its calibration on the GL / DX pair |
26	| `godot/tests/capture_glow.gd`, `capture_hint.gd`, `capture_hydrant.gd` | windowed in-engine captures (viewport reads) behind every pixel value in TEST-REPORT |
27	| `scripts/run-test.sh` | the test wrapper (timeout, pinned fps, log, fails on SHADER / SCRIPT ERROR) |
28	
29	### Run the tests
30	
31	```
32	# from the repository root; Godot 4.7 on PATH as `godot` (macOS: ~/Downloads/Godot.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot)
33	godot --headless --path godot --import                      # once, after cloning
34	./scripts/run-test.sh test_hose_glow.gd 30                  # 15 checks; also at 60 and 144
35	./scripts/run-test.sh test_hose_glow.gd 60
36	./scripts/run-test.sh test_hose_glow.gd 144
37	./scripts/run-test.sh test_materials.gd 60                  # 35 checks
38	./scripts/run-test.sh test_game.gd 60                       # A2 baseline: 41 checks
39	./scripts/run-test.sh test_keyboard.gd 60                   # 14
40	./scripts/run-test.sh test_audio.gd 60                      # 12 / 14 with the fps pin (TEST-REPORT baseline explains the two)
41	./scripts/run-test.sh check_props.gd 60                     # A3: RESULT: PASS
42	```
43	
44	Logs land in `logs/`. **Play it:** `godot --path godot`; W next to the big fire starts the water and the glow. **See the hydrants:** open `godot/project.godot` in the editor and run `scenes3d/props_room.tscn`; the hint experiment is `scenes3d/hint_experiment.tscn`.
45	
46	### Known limitations
47	
48	- Under this project's **GL Compatibility** renderer the hint experiment's two quads are identical: 3D is shaded in sRGB space, so `source_color` changes nothing on screen here. The hint is still required and the prediction for Forward+/Mobile stands (TEST-REPORT).
49	- The **roughness and normal-strength sliders show no visible difference** under the props room's single sun; the sampled pixel moves 1–3 levels. A second light would be the next experiment.
50	- The hydrant mesh is the basic A3 one; "improve the structure of the hydrant" is my next step, outside this assignment (the A3 model files must not change).
51	- The glow is on the sprite only; the code-drawn rescue bag stays orange (checked by a controlled capture, since rescues come after the hose in play).
52	- `Engine.time_scale = 0.5` by eye is an **open** human check (TEST-REPORT Open items).
53	- Headless tests prove parse, uniform names and types, timing and material wiring; every look is a human check in TEST-REPORT.
54	
55	### Film
56	
57	Brutalist `godot-gamedev` explainer, `walker` mode, native 4K, 6 min 22 s, 32 MB, narrated by Liam: *Extinguisho's Hand-Written Shaders*. Source shown: revision `e8c2a30` (no file under `godot/` changed after it).
58	
59	- **Link (Northeastern SharePoint, course media storage):** https://northeastern-my.sharepoint.com/:f:/g/personal/pulaparty_s_northeastern_edu/IgCzqn1JsKZORIVL8gL8oe0KAUD2cXE4KHod2yt1IJlg6G8?e=DaGz30
60	- **File:** `claude-liam-walker-ninja-firefighter-joe-a5-gamedev.mp4`
61	- **SHA-256:** `67d77d0a7632e78b341f2ee3e997df2f2e7bcf3e902dea5f263ee1bfc45a52da`
62	- **Film source** (approved script, beat sheet, evidence ledger, capture and build scripts): [`youtube/claude-liam-walker-ninja-firefighter-joe-a5-gamedev/`](youtube/claude-liam-walker-ninja-firefighter-joe-a5-gamedev/). The MP4 and the Movie Maker AVI are not in git (course rule).
63	
64	## Assignment 3 — first 3D assets
65	
66	Three props for my game, built in Blender by directing Claude Code through the Blender MCP, exported as `.glb`, and shown together in a small Godot 3D scene: a **fire hydrant**, the **rescue bag** (a backpack — it rides on Extinguisho's back), and a **flame** (the game's main hazard). # walker-ninja-firefighter-joe

My CSYE 7270 game, built up one assignment at a time. Each assignment is a git tag: **`a2`** (generated art, sound and music; submitted from the class repo at commit `50a1797`), **`a3`** (three simple 3D props), **`a5`** (two hand-written shaders, their materials, and the Godot shading language).

## Assignment 5 — shaders, materials, and the Godot shading language

Two shaders I typed by hand, and the materials that use them. **Extinguisho glows pale blue while he hoses** (a `canvas_item` shader on his sprite, driven from the game's `player.hosing` state by a small script Claude Code wrote), and the **A3 hydrant gets a real surface** (a `spatial` shader that reads Poly Haven's rusty-metal colour, roughness and normal maps, with two materials: freshly painted and rusty). A third small shader is the **hint experiment** (one grey strip sampled as colour and as data), and a fourth is Godot's own, generated from a StandardMaterial3D, which I read and annotated.

**Docs:** [CHANGE-BRIEF](CHANGE-BRIEF.md) (v1 committed before any shader or prompt; Revisions 1–4) · [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) (agent draft, then my review) · [`a5/`](a5/): [TEST-REPORT](a5/TEST-REPORT.md) · [LANGUAGE-NOTES](a5/LANGUAGE-NOTES.md) · [STANDARD-GENERATED-ANNOTATED](a5/STANDARD-GENERATED-ANNOTATED.md) · [FRICTIONAL](a5/FRICTIONAL.md) · [SOURCES](a5/SOURCES.md) · evidence (captures, mutation logs, playtest screenshots) in `a5/evidence/`, prompts in `a5/prompts/`, `claude -p` transcripts in `a5/sessions/` · [`godot/MATERIALS.md`](godot/MATERIALS.md) (the audit) · texture credits in [`godot/art/textures/rusty_metal_sheet/ATTRIBUTION.md`](godot/art/textures/rusty_metal_sheet/ATTRIBUTION.md).

**Versions:** Godot 4.7.2 stable, GL Compatibility renderer · macOS 26.6.2 (Apple M1) · Claude Code 2.1.285 (`claude-fable-5-1`) for the driver, tests, audit and film.

### What this assignment added

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `godot/shaders/hose_glow.gdshader` | **mine**, 8 lines: `glow` (float, `hint_range`) and `glow_color` (`source_color`); the colour line `COLOR.rgb = mix(COLOR.rgb, glow_color.rgb, glow);` |
| `godot/features/player/hose_glow.gd` (+ 2-line hook in `player.gd`) | the driver (agent): one `ShaderMaterial` on the sprite; `glow` ramps 0 → band in 0.25 s, breathes 0.4–0.8 at 1 s while hosing, ramps to 0 in 0.25 s after; scaled `delta`, never writes game state |
| `godot/shaders/hydrant_surface.gdshader` | **mine**, 25 lines: `albedo_tex : source_color`, `rough_tex : hint_default_white`, `normal_tex : hint_normal`; five dials in `paint` and `surface` groups |
| `godot/materials/hydrant_fresh.tres`, `hydrant_rusty.tres` | two materials, one shader: rust 0.1 / roughness 0.7 vs 0.9 / 1.4; fresh bound through the glb importer's Use External, rusty as a surface override on a second hydrant in `props_room.tscn` |
| `godot/art/textures/rusty_metal_sheet/` | Poly Haven *Rusty Metal Sheet* (Amal Kumar, CC0), `diff` / `rough` / `nor_gl` bound, `nor_dx` for calibration only; explicit `.import` settings; `ATTRIBUTION.md` |
| `godot/shaders/hint_experiment.gdshader`, `materials/hint_as_*.tres`, `scenes3d/hint_experiment.tscn`, `tests/write_grey_strip.gd`, `art/hint/grey_3x1.png` | **mine** (the shader): the hint experiment, Linear tonemap at exposure 1.0 |
| `godot/shaders/standard_generated.gdshader`, `scenes3d/scratch_standard.tscn` | Godot's generated shader from a converted StandardMaterial3D; nothing in the game uses it |
| `godot/tests/test_hose_glow.gd` | agent: 15 checks through real input events at 30 / 60 / 144 fps |
| `godot/tests/test_materials.gd`, `normal_map_check.gd`, `calibrate_normal_maps.gd` | agent audit test (35 checks), the assignment's curl check, its calibration on the GL / DX pair |
| `godot/tests/capture_glow.gd`, `capture_hint.gd`, `capture_hydrant.gd` | windowed in-engine captures (viewport reads) behind every pixel value in TEST-REPORT |
| `scripts/run-test.sh` | the test wrapper (timeout, pinned fps, log, fails on SHADER / SCRIPT ERROR) |

### Run the tests

```
# from the repository root; Godot 4.7 on PATH as `godot` (macOS: ~/Downloads/Godot.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot)
godot --headless --path godot --import                      # once, after cloning
./scripts/run-test.sh test_hose_glow.gd 30                  # 15 checks; also at 60 and 144
./scripts/run-test.sh test_hose_glow.gd 60
./scripts/run-test.sh test_hose_glow.gd 144
./scripts/run-test.sh test_materials.gd 60                  # 35 checks
./scripts/run-test.sh test_game.gd 60                       # A2 baseline: 41 checks
./scripts/run-test.sh test_keyboard.gd 60                   # 14

./scripts/run-test.sh check_props.gd 60                     # A3: RESULT: PASS
```

Logs land in `logs/`. **Play it:** `godot --path godot`; W next to the big fire starts the water and the glow. **See the hydrants:** open `godot/project.godot` in the editor and run `scenes3d/props_room.tscn`; the hint experiment is `scenes3d/hint_experiment.tscn`.

## Assignment 2 — asset slice

An asset slice for CSYE 7270 Assignment 2: **Extinguisho**, a deadpan ninja firefighter, has 40 seconds to rescue a person and a dog from two burning buildings: kung-fu jump over flames, hose the fire blocking the way, toss the survivors into his bag, and escape off the roof. The art (and, in progress, the sound and music) is generated with generative models and wired into a playable Godot scene.


## Started from

My Assignment 1 project, `walker-jumpman-joe` (a firefighter rescue platformer), which extended [nikbearbrown/walker-jumpman](https://github.com/nikbearbrown/walker-jumpman) ("First Steps" starter). The Godot project in `godot/` was copied on 2026-10-01 (control and retry engine, state machine, level, hose and rescue mechanics, timer, tests). See SOURCES.md.

## Engine

Godot **4.7.2** stable (GL Compatibility renderer), macOS.

## Run it

1. Install Godot 4.7 or newer.
2. Open `godot/project.godot` in Godot and press Play, **or** from a terminal:
   ```
   <path-to-Godot> --path godot
   ```
   On macOS with Godot in Applications, double-click `walker-jumpman.command`.

Automated tests (from `godot/`):
```
<path-to-Godot> --headless --path . -s tests/test_game.gd       # 41 checks
<path-to-Godot> --headless --path . -s tests/test_keyboard.gd
<path-to-Godot> --headless --path . -s tests/test_audio.gd      # one sound per event; mute changes nothing
<path-to-Godot> --path . -s tests/capture_game.gd               # screenshots of every state -> evidence/screens/
```

## Controls

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| A / D or ← / → | move |
| Space | jump |
| W | hose the blocking fire (when close) |
| R | retry |
| Esc or P | pause |
| Enter | start / resume / play again |
| M | main menu (from pause or the end card) |
| N | mute / unmute music |
| B | mute / unmute sound effects |

## What the slice demonstrates

- **Character:** 11 generated state images swapped by game state: idle, run, flying-kick jump, meditating fall, landing, hose, rescue grab, upward toss, burned, respawn stance, and a bow at the end. Facing left mirrors the art. Collision box 20×40 (CHARACTER-SHEET.md, collision overlay).
- **Environment:** a generated smoky city skyline (ENV-BG v2) behind the level, and generated flames (ENV-FIRE) on every fire hazard; the fire blocking the person shrinks as it's hosed.
- **Failure punchline and win:** on a fire death (held 2 s; R retries at once) the generated DEVASTATED close-up pops up next to "The fire got you."; on the win, the bow close-up pops up.
- **Sound:** generated sound effects on real game events: jump, hose, rescue toss, fire death, level complete. Each fires exactly once per event (`tests/test_audio.gd`). Muting changes nothing in play.
- **Music:** a 16-bar, 150 BPM generated loop (ElevenLabs Music) that pauses on pause, dips on a fire death, continues on retry, and stops on the win (`tests/test_audio.gd`).
- **Design and evidence:** CONCEPT.md, STORYBOARD.md, CHARACTER-SHEET.md, a2/CHANGE-BRIEF.md (plan and predictions; moved from the root for Assignment 5, which needs its own brief at that path), SOURCES.md (models and asset log), TEST-REPORT.md, ../FRICTIONAL.md (design log), rejected outputs in `rejected/`, in-engine screenshots in `evidence/screens-web/`.

## Known limitations

- The character's face doesn't read at game size (64 px); attitude comes through the poses. The burned pose is dark and subtle on the dark background.
- The level, survivors, rescue bag, and HUD are code-drawn (from A1), not generated.
- Muted, the fire death is understood mainly through its on-screen text ("The fire got you."); the burn sound carries part of that moment (muted playtest).
- The run is slower and the jump floatier than A1 (changed after playtest 2); a fire death holds 2 s (playtest 3), longer than A1's 1 s retry.
- The background was regenerated (ENV-BG v2, cool blue-gray) after playtest 3 so the red-and-yellow character stands out; the burning city now reads through smoke columns and the game's flames rather than an orange sky.
- ChatGPT does not expose seeds, so regenerating an image from its logged prompt gives a similar, not identical, result.

106	func _add_solid(rect: Rect2) -> void:
107		var body := StaticBody2D.new()
108		body.position = rect.position + rect.size / 2
109		body.collision_layer = 1
110		body.collision_mask = 2
111		var shape := RectangleShape2D.new()
112		shape.size = rect.size
113		var collision := CollisionShape2D.new()
114		collision.shape = shape
115		body.add_child(collision)

118	func _add_area(rect: Rect2, layer: int, spikes: bool) -> Area2D:
119		var area := Area2D.new()
120		area.position = rect.position
121		area.collision_layer = layer
122		area.collision_mask = 2
123		if spikes:
124			# Three exact triangular trigger silhouettes; no oversized invisible box.
125			for i in range(3):
126				var triangle := CollisionPolygon2D.new()
127				var x := float(i) * rect.size.x / 3.0
128				triangle.polygon = PackedVector2Array([Vector2(x, rect.size.y), Vector2(x + 4, 0), Vector2(x + 8, rect.size.y)])
129				area.add_child(triangle)
130		else:
131			var collision := CollisionShape2D.new()
132			var shape := RectangleShape2D.new()
133			shape.size = rect.size
134			collision.shape = shape
135			collision.position = rect.size / 2.0
136			area.add_child(collision)
137		add_child(area)
138		return area

213	func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
214		if state == State.DYING:
215			retry_remaining -= delta
216			if retry_remaining <= 0:
217				restart_attempt()
218		elif state == State.PLAYING:
219			elapsed += delta
220			var fell := player.position.y > float(level.fall_y)
221			var timed_out := elapsed >= float(level.time_limit)
222			var hit_fire := false
223			for hazard in hazard_areas:
224				if hazard.overlaps_body(player):
225					hit_fire = true
226			# The blocking fire is lethal + blocks the path until FULLY hosed. Its kill-zone
227			# shrinks from the top with the flames (see fire_height), but the base stays lethal
228			# until the fire is completely out -- so walking in mid-extinguish still kills.
229			if fire_active and level.has("blocking_fire"):
230				var bf0: Array = level.blocking_fire
231				var fire_top: float = (float(bf0[1]) + float(bf0[3])) - fire_height()
232				var half_w: float = Player.BOX.x / 2.0
233				if player.position.x + half_w > float(bf0[0]) and player.position.x - half_w < float(bf0[0]) + float(bf0[2]) and player.position.y > fire_top and player.position.y - Player.BOX.y < float(bf0[1]) + float(bf0[3]):
234					hit_fire = true
235			var fatal := fell or timed_out or hit_fire
236			if fatal:
237				death_reason = "Out of time!" if timed_out else ("You fell." if fell else "The fire got you.")
238			# Hose: tap W within range of the blocking fire -> water pours ~4 s -> fire out.
239			near_fire = false
240			if fire_active and level.has("blocking_fire"):
241				var bf: Array = level.blocking_fire
242				near_fire = player.is_on_floor() and player.position.x > float(bf[0]) - 50.0 and player.position.x < float(bf[0]) + float(bf[2]) + 10.0 and player.position.y < float(bf[1]) + float(bf[3]) + 20.0 and player.position.y > float(bf[1]) - 40.0
243				var water: bool = player.test_water_pressed if player.test_control else Input.is_action_just_pressed("water")
244				if player.test_control:
245					player.test_water_pressed = false
246				if water and near_fire and extinguish_ticks == 0:
247					extinguish_ticks = EXTINGUISH_TICKS
248					water_ticks = EXTINGUISH_TICKS + 60  # water lingers ~1 s after it is out
249					play_sfx("hose")
250			if extinguish_ticks > 0:
251				extinguish_ticks -= 1
252				if extinguish_ticks == 0:
253					fire_active = false
254			if water_ticks > 0:
255				water_ticks -= 1
256			player.hosing = water_ticks > 0
257			# Touch to rescue -- only while NOT in a fatal state, so you can't rescue THROUGH fire.
258			if not fatal:
259				for s in survivors:
260					if not s.rescued and s.area.overlaps_body(player):
261						s.rescued = true
262						s.area.set_deferred("monitoring", false)
263						rescued_count += 1
264						player.rescued = rescued_count
265						player.bag_types.append(s.type)
266						player.bag_in_flight += 1
267						player.play_actions([["grab", GRAB_TICKS], ["toss", TOSS_UP_TICKS]])
268						flights.append({"type": s.type, "from": Vector2(s.x, s.y), "t": 0})
269						play_sfx("rescue")
270						saved_popup_ticks = 55
271						saved_popup_pos = Vector2(s.x - 18.0, s.y - 34.0)
272			var all_rescued := rescued_count >= survivors.size()
273			var at_exit := goal.overlaps_body(player) and player.is_on_floor()
274			if at_exit and not all_rescued:
275				locked_cue_ticks = 45  # flash "rescue everyone first"
276			if locked_cue_ticks > 0:
277				locked_cue_ticks -= 1
278			if saved_popup_ticks > 0:
279				saved_popup_ticks -= 1
280			if contact_settle_ticks > 0:
281				contact_settle_ticks -= 1
282			else:
283				# Exit completes only when BOTH survivors are rescued AND reached on foot.
284				# State machine unchanged; only the COMPLETE condition gains "both rescued".
285				resolve_contacts(fatal, at_exit and all_rescued)
286			camera.position.x = clampf(player.position.x + 100, 320, float(level.width) - 320)
287		if state == State.COMPLETE:
288			complete_ticks += 1
289		for fl in flights:
290			fl.t += 1
291			if fl.t == GRAB_TICKS:  # toss starts: launch from his raised hand, straight up
292				fl.launch = player.position + Vector2(0.0, -62.0)
293				fl.apex = fl.launch + Vector2(0.0, -TOSS_HEIGHT)
294			if fl.t >= GRAB_TICKS + TOSS_UP_TICKS + TOSS_DOWN_TICKS:
295				player.bag_in_flight = maxi(player.bag_in_flight - 1, 0)
296				player.queue_redraw()
297		flights = flights.filter(func(fl): return fl.t < GRAB_TICKS + TOSS_UP_TICKS + TOSS_DOWN_TICKS)
298		if is_instance_valid(hud):
299			hud.queue_redraw()
300		queue_redraw()  # refresh the level's own dynamic draw: survivors vanish, SAVED! animates, exit unlocks

483	func _draw_flights() -> void:
484		var ink := Color("25354a")
485		for fl in flights:
486			var t: int = fl.t
487			var from: Vector2 = fl.from + Vector2(0.0, -12.0)
488			var launch: Vector2 = fl.get("launch", from)
489			var apex: Vector2 = fl.get("apex", from + Vector2(0.0, -TOSS_HEIGHT))
490			var bag: Vector2 = Player.BAG.get(player.pose, Player.BAG.idle)
491			var into := player.position + Vector2(bag.x * player.facing, bag.y - 6.0)
492			var pos := from
493			var spin := 0.0
494			if t >= GRAB_TICKS + TOSS_UP_TICKS:
495				var k := float(t - GRAB_TICKS - TOSS_UP_TICKS) / float(TOSS_DOWN_TICKS)
496				pos = Vector2(lerpf(apex.x, into.x, k), lerpf(apex.y, into.y, k * k))
497				spin = float(t) * 0.5
498			elif t >= GRAB_TICKS:
499				var k := float(t - GRAB_TICKS) / float(TOSS_UP_TICKS)
500				pos = launch.lerp(apex, 1.0 - (1.0 - k) * (1.0 - k))
501				spin = float(t) * 0.5
502			draw_set_transform(pos, spin, Vector2.ONE)
503			if fl.type == "dog":
504				draw_rect(Rect2(-7, -3, 12, 7), ink)
505				draw_rect(Rect2(-6, -2, 10, 5), Color("d59243"))
506				draw_circle(Vector2(6, -3), 4.0, ink)
507				draw_circle(Vector2(6, -3), 3.0, Color("d59243"))
508			else:

521	# Two buses so music and effects mute separately (N / B). Streams load only if the file exists,
522	# so a missing sound leaves the game unchanged.
523	func _setup_audio() -> void:
524		for bus in ["Music", "SFX"]:
525			if AudioServer.get_bus_index(bus) == -1:
526				AudioServer.add_bus()
527				AudioServer.set_bus_name(AudioServer.bus_count - 1, bus)
528		for id in SFX_FILES:
529			var p := AudioStreamPlayer.new()
530			p.bus = "SFX"
531			var path := "res://audio/%s.ogg" % SFX_FILES[id]
532			if ResourceLoader.exists(path):
533				p.stream = load(path)
534			add_child(p)
535			sfx_players[id] = p
536			sfx_counts[id] = 0
537		music = AudioStreamPlayer.new()
538		music.bus = "Music"
539		if ResourceLoader.exists(MUSIC_FILE):
540			music.stream = load(MUSIC_FILE)
541			music.stream.loop = true
542		add_child(music)

558	# Music follows the state (CHANGE-BRIEF "Music behavior"): plays while playing, pauses in place on
559	# pause, dips under the burn while DYING and comes back on retry (no restart), stops on COMPLETE,
560	# off in the menu.
561	func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
562		if music == null or music.stream == null:
563			return
564		match state:
565			State.PLAYING:
566				music.volume_db = 0.0
567				music.stream_paused = false
568				if not music.playing:
569					music.play()
570			State.DYING:
571				music.volume_db = MUSIC_DIP_DB
572			State.PAUSED:
573				music.stream_paused = true
574			_:
575				music.stop()

extends CharacterBody2D

signal jumped  # emitted once per real jump (the session plays SFX-JUMP; sound never feeds back)

const Tuning = preload("res://features/player/tuning.gd")
const HoseGlow = preload("res://features/player/hose_glow.gd")  # A5: glow material on `sprite`, driven from `hosing`
var tuning = Tuning.new()
var enabled: bool = false
var tick: int = 0
var last_floor_tick: int = -1000
var jump_request_tick: int = -1000
var opportunity_consumed: bool = false
var require_jump_release: bool = true
var facing: float = 1.0
var rescued: int = 0  # survivors in the rescue bag (set by session; used for drawing)
var bag_types: Array = []  # survivor types riding in the bag, e.g. ["person","dog"] (set by session)
var jumps: int = 0
var test_control: bool = false
var test_axis: float = 0.0
var test_jump_pressed: bool = false
var test_jump_held: bool = false
var test_water_pressed: bool = false  # hose input hook for the scripted route / tests
# Extinguisho art: one static generated image per state, swapped in (visual only; never read by gameplay).
const ART_DIR := "res://art/character/"
const BOX := Vector2(20, 40)   # collision box; feet at the origin (CHARACTER-SHEET, collision option A)
const LAND_TICKS := 20         # landing pose holds this long after real air time (was 8: too fast to see)
const NOZZLE := Vector2(33, -27.5)  # hose nozzle tip in the hose pose (game px, facing right): the water starts here
# Rescue bag center per pose (game px, facing right): on his back at the hip, measured on each image.
const BAG := {"idle": Vector2(-10, -30), "respawn": Vector2(-13, -20), "run": Vector2(-8, -21),
	"jump_crouch": Vector2(-9, -30), "rising": Vector2(-10, -18), "falling": Vector2(-12, -16),
	"landing": Vector2(-8, -20), "hose": Vector2(-10, -19), "grab": Vector2(-10, -27),
	"toss": Vector2(-10, -31), "burned": Vector2(-10, -30), "celebrate": Vector2(-9, -27)}
var pose: String = "idle"
var art: Node2D
var sprite: Sprite2D
var textures := {}
var anchors := {}
var jumped_this_air: bool = false
var air_ticks: int = 0
var land_ticks: int = 0
var was_on_floor: bool = true
var hosing: bool = false        # water is pouring (set by session)
var bag_in_flight: int = 0      # survivors still flying toward the bag (set by session); their heads appear on landing
var action_queue: Array = []    # timed poses that override movement, e.g. [["grab", 15], ["toss", 27]]
var action_cancel_on_move: bool = false

func _ready() -> void:
	name = "Player"
	collision_layer = 2
	collision_mask = 1
	floor_snap_length = 1.0
	var shape := RectangleShape2D.new()
	shape.size = BOX
	var collider := CollisionShape2D.new()
	collider.shape = shape
	collider.position = Vector2(0, -BOX.y / 2.0)
	add_child(collider)
	var info: Dictionary = JSON.parse_string(FileAccess.get_file_as_string(ART_DIR + "anchors.json"))
	anchors = info.anchors
	for state in anchors:
		textures[state] = load(ART_DIR + state + ".png")
	art = Node2D.new()
	art.show_behind_parent = true  # the code-drawn rescue bag stays on top of the art
	add_child(art)
	sprite = Sprite2D.new()
	sprite.centered = false
	art.add_child(sprite)
	show_pose("idle")
	add_child(HoseGlow.new())  # visual only; the driver reads `hosing` and writes the shader's `glow`

# Swap the state image. The anchor (bottom-center of the collision box in texture px)
# lands on the origin; the holder's negative x scale mirrors the art when facing left.
func show_pose(state: String) -> void:
	pose = state
	sprite.texture = textures[state]
	var a: Array = anchors[state]
	sprite.position = -Vector2(a[0], a[1])
	art.scale = Vector2(0.5 * facing, 0.5)
	queue_redraw()  # the bag follows the pose

# Timed state poses (grab, toss, respawn), played in order and held for their tick count.
func play_actions(steps: Array, cancel_on_move: bool = false) -> void:
	action_queue = steps.duplicate(true)
	action_cancel_on_move = cancel_on_move
	show_pose(action_queue[0][0])

func _update_pose() -> void:
	var on_floor := is_on_floor()
	if on_floor:
		if not was_on_floor and air_ticks > 10:
			land_ticks = LAND_TICKS
		air_ticks = 0
		jumped_this_air = false
	else:
		air_ticks += 1
	was_on_floor = on_floor
	if land_ticks > 0:
		land_ticks -= 1
	if not action_queue.is_empty() and action_cancel_on_move and (absf(velocity.x) > 8.0 or not on_floor):
		action_queue.clear()
	if not action_queue.is_empty():
		show_pose(action_queue[0][0])
		action_queue[0][1] -= 1
		if action_queue[0][1] <= 0:
			action_queue.pop_front()
	elif not on_floor:
		# A jump is one flying kick all the way; walking off a ledge is the meditating fall.
		show_pose("rising" if jumped_this_air else "falling")
	elif land_ticks > 0:
		show_pose("landing")
	elif absf(velocity.x) > 8.0:
		show_pose("run")
	elif hosing:
		show_pose("hose")
	else:
		show_pose("idle")

func reset_at(spawn: Vector2) -> void:
	position = spawn
	velocity = Vector2.ZERO
	last_floor_tick = -1000
	jump_request_tick = -1000
	opportunity_consumed = false
	require_jump_release = true
	test_jump_pressed = false
	jumps = 0
	rescued = 0
	bag_types.clear()
	jumped_this_air = false
	air_ticks = 0
	land_ticks = 0
	was_on_floor = true
	hosing = false
	bag_in_flight = 0
	play_actions([["respawn", 30]], true)  # snaps into the ready stance; any movement ends it
	queue_redraw()

func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
	if not enabled:
		return
	tick += 1
	var axis := test_axis if test_control else Input.get_axis("move_left", "move_right")
	var held := test_jump_held if test_control else Input.is_action_pressed("jump")
	var pressed := test_jump_pressed if test_control else Input.is_action_just_pressed("jump")
	test_jump_pressed = false
	if not held:
		require_jump_release = false
	if is_on_floor() and velocity.y >= 0.0:
		last_floor_tick = tick
		opportunity_consumed = false
	if pressed and not require_jump_release:
		jump_request_tick = tick
	var rate: float = tuning.acceleration if not is_zero_approx(axis) else tuning.deceleration
	velocity.x = move_toward(velocity.x, axis * tuning.speed, rate * delta)
	if not is_zero_approx(axis):
		facing = signf(axis)
	velocity.y = minf(velocity.y + tuning.gravity * delta, tuning.terminal_velocity)
	if not opportunity_consumed and tick - last_floor_tick <= tuning.coyote_ticks and tick - jump_request_tick <= tuning.buffer_ticks:
		velocity.y = tuning.jump_velocity
		opportunity_consumed = true
		jump_request_tick = -1000
		jumps += 1
		jumped_this_air = true
		jumped.emit()
	move_and_slide()
	position.x = maxf(position.x, 10.0)
	_update_pose()
	queue_redraw()

func _draw() -> void:
	# The body is the generated art (sprite above). Only the rescue bag is still code-drawn:
	# the art has no bag, and rescued survivors ride in it (person or dog head per rescue).
	# Same drawing as Assignment 1, doubled, placed per pose on his back. Hidden until the
	# first rescue, so the empty bag doesn't cover the generated art.
	if bag_types.is_empty():
		return
	var f := facing                 # +1 right, -1 left
	var c: Vector2 = BAG.get(pose, BAG.idle)
	draw_set_transform(Vector2(c.x * f, c.y), 0.0, Vector2(2.0, 2.0))
	var ink := Color("1b2a3f")      # outline
	var skin := Color("e8b98f")     # face
	var bag_col := Color("e67e22")  # orange rescue duffel
	var bag_dark := Color("b8621b") # bag seam
	draw_rect(Rect2(-4.5, -4.5, 9, 9), ink)
	draw_rect(Rect2(-3.5, -3.5, 7, 7), bag_col)
	draw_rect(Rect2(-3.5, -3.5, 7, 2), bag_dark)
	# rescued survivors ride in the bag — a clear head per rescue (grows as you save more)
	for i in range(bag_types.size() - bag_in_flight):
		var hx := (-1.0 + float(i) * 4.5) * f
		var hyy := -7.0
		if String(bag_types[i]) == "dog":
			draw_colored_polygon(PackedVector2Array([Vector2(hx-3, hyy-1), Vector2(hx-2, hyy-6), Vector2(hx+0.5, hyy-1)]), Color("6b4420"))  # left ear
			draw_colored_polygon(PackedVector2Array([Vector2(hx+0.5, hyy-1), Vector2(hx+2, hyy-6), Vector2(hx+3, hyy-1)]), Color("6b4420"))  # right ear
			draw_circle(Vector2(hx, hyy), 3.2, Color("8a5a2b"))       # dog head
			draw_circle(Vector2(hx + 1.2 * f, hyy + 0.5), 0.9, ink)  # snout/eye
		else:
			draw_circle(Vector2(hx, hyy), 3.2, skin)                 # person head
			draw_rect(Rect2(hx - 3.0, hyy - 3.6, 6.0, 2.2), Color("3a2f1a"))  # hair
			draw_circle(Vector2(hx + 1.2 * f, hyy), 0.8, ink)        # eye

extends Node
# Hose glow driver (CHANGE-BRIEF A2/A3, Revision 3). Presentation only: it reads player.hosing
# and writes one shader parameter on player.sprite. It never writes game state.

const SHADER := preload("res://shaders/hose_glow.gdshader")  # hand-written; not edited here
const PARAM := "glow"
const RAMP_SECONDS := 0.25   # R3: the ramps move at 1/RAMP_SECONDS per game second (0 -> 1 in 0.25 s)
const BREATH_CENTRE := 0.6   # Revision 3: while hosing, glow breathes 0.4..0.8 ...
const BREATH_AMPLITUDE := 0.2
const BREATH_PERIOD := 1.0   # ... with a 1.0 s period, in game seconds
var glow := 0.0
var hose_time := 0.0         # game seconds since hosing began (driver clock, not the shader's TIME)
var material: ShaderMaterial

func _ready() -> void:
	name = "HoseGlow"
	# One material per player instance (R8), on the sprite only (F5): the code-drawn rescue
	# bag and survivor heads are drawn on the body, not on the sprite, so they keep their colours.
	material = ShaderMaterial.new()
	material.shader = SHADER
	get_parent().sprite.material = material
	material.set_shader_parameter(PARAM, glow)

func _process(delta: float) -> void:
	# _process runs after this frame's physics ticks, so it sees the session's fresh `hosing`.
	# delta is scaled game time (R4, R6): the ramps and the breathing run on it at any frame rate.
	# move_toward from the current value: a state change mid-ramp reverses from where it is (R7).
	var target := 0.0
	if get_parent().hosing:
		# t = 0 on the first frame hosing is seen (target 0.6), then accumulates per frame.
		target = BREATH_CENTRE + BREATH_AMPLITUDE * sin(TAU * hose_time / BREATH_PERIOD)
		hose_time += delta
	else:
		hose_time = 0.0
	glow = move_toward(glow, target, delta / RAMP_SECONDS)
	material.set_shader_parameter(PARAM, glow)

25	# Records {g: glow uniform, d: process delta, h: player.hosing} once per _process frame, after
26	# everyone else's _process (priority 100). It only reads; it never touches the driver.
27	class Sampler extends Node:
28		var game: Node2D
29		var samples: Array = []
30		func _process(delta: float) -> void:
31			if not is_instance_valid(game) or game.player == null or game.player.sprite == null:
32				return

95	# Every step between a and b (inclusive) moves in `dir` (+1 up, -1 down), never backwards,
96	# and by at most delta / RAMP (+ EPS). Returns {ok, worst_step}.
97	func monotone(a: int, b: int, dir: float) -> Dictionary:
98		var ok := a >= 0 and b > a
99		var worst := 0.0
100		for i in range(a + 1, b + 1):
101			var step: float = (S()[i].g - S()[i - 1].g) * dir
102			var max_step: float = S()[i].d / RAMP + EPS
103			worst = maxf(worst, step)
104			if step < -EPS or step > max_step:
105				ok = false
106		return {"ok": ok, "worst_step": worst}

108	func all_in_band(a: int, b: int) -> bool:
109		if a < 0 or b < a:
110			return false
111		for i in range(a, b + 1):
112			if not in_band(S()[i].g):
113				return false
114		return true

116	# Indices of the strict local maxima of g in [a, b] (a > 0, b < size - 1). A tie with the next
117	# sample counts once, on the first of the pair (at 30 fps the peak at t = 0.25 s falls between
118	# two samples that are equal up to rounding).

120		var peaks: Array[int] = []

122			if S()[i].g > S()[i - 1].g and S()[i].g >= S()[i + 1].g:
123				peaks.append(i)
124		return peaks

130			lo = minf(lo, S()[i].g)
131			hi = maxf(hi, S()[i].g)
132		return {"min": lo, "max": hi}

extends SceneTree
# A5 hose glow (CHANGE-BRIEF Part A): the shader's interface and the driver's rules, headless.
# The hosing state is driven through the real game loop and synthetic key events (W, R), never
# by calling the driver. The uniform is read every frame by a Sampler node whose process_priority
# is high, so it runs after every other _process in the frame (the driver included).
# Run at 30, 60 and 144 fps: scripts/run-test.sh test_hose_glow.gd <fps>.
# Revision 3: the hold is a breathing band 0.4..0.8 with a 1.0 s period instead of a flat 1.0;
# the hold assertions (in-band, maxima, period) and the ramp targets follow it.
# What this cannot see: pixels. Headless Godot draws nothing (CLAUDE.md, Headless facts).
const Game = preload("res://game/session.gd")
const SHADER_PATH := "res://shaders/hose_glow.gdshader"
const DRIVER_PATH := "res://features/player/hose_glow.gd"
const RAMP := 0.25     # R3: ramp rate is 1/RAMP per game second
const BAND_LO := 0.4   # Revision 3: while hosing, glow breathes 0.6 + 0.2 sin(2π t) ...
const BAND_HI := 0.8
const PERIOD := 1.0    # ... with a 1.0 s period in game seconds
const EPS := 1e-5
const BAND_EPS := 1e-4   # membership tolerance for the band
const REACH_EPS := 0.01  # how close the sampled signal must come to 0.4 and 0.8 (sampling at 30 fps loses < 0.002)
var game: Node2D
var sampler: Sampler
var results: Array[Dictionary] = []
var failures := 0

# Records {g: glow uniform, d: process delta, h: player.hosing} once per _process frame, after
# everyone else's _process (priority 100). It only reads; it never touches the driver.
class Sampler extends Node:
	var game: Node2D
	var samples: Array = []
	func _process(delta: float) -> void:
		if not is_instance_valid(game) or game.player == null or game.player.sprite == null:
			return
		var mat: Material = game.player.sprite.material
		var g: float = float(mat.get_shader_parameter("glow")) if mat is ShaderMaterial else -1.0
		samples.append({"g": g, "d": delta, "h": game.player.hosing})

func _initialize() -> void:
	call_deferred("run")

func steps(n: int) -> void:
	for i in range(n):
		await physics_frame
		await process_frame

# Synthetic key event through Godot Input, the path test_keyboard.gd already proves reaches
# Input.is_action_just_pressed in physics (W) and _unhandled_input (R) headlessly.
func key(code: Key, pressed: bool) -> void:
	var event := InputEventKey.new()
	event.keycode = code
	event.physical_keycode = code
	event.pressed = pressed
	Input.parse_input_event(event)

func check(id: String, condition: bool, observed: Dictionary) -> void:
	results.append({"id": id, "status": "PASS" if condition else "FAIL", "observed": observed})
	print(JSON.stringify(results.back()))
	if not condition:
		failures += 1

func fresh() -> void:
	if is_instance_valid(game):
		game.queue_free()
		await process_frame
	game = Game.new()
	game.test_mode = true
	root.add_child(game)
	game.start_session()          # real input: player.test_control stays false
	sampler.game = game
	sampler.samples.clear()
	game.player.position = Vector2(1220, 240)  # on B1-PW, in hose range (same spot as test_game.gd)
	await steps(3)

func S() -> Array:
	return sampler.samples

func in_band(g: float) -> bool:
	return g >= BAND_LO - BAND_EPS and g <= BAND_HI + BAND_EPS

func zero(g: float) -> bool:
	return is_zero_approx(g)

func first_from(from: int, pred: Callable) -> int:
	for i in range(from, S().size()):
		if pred.call(S()[i]):
			return i
	return -1

func last_before(limit: int, pred: Callable) -> int:
	var found := -1
	for i in range(0, limit):
		if pred.call(S()[i]):
			found = i
	return found

# Every step between a and b (inclusive) moves in `dir` (+1 up, -1 down), never backwards,
# and by at most delta / RAMP (+ EPS). Returns {ok, worst_step}.
func monotone(a: int, b: int, dir: float) -> Dictionary:
	var ok := a >= 0 and b > a
	var worst := 0.0
	for i in range(a + 1, b + 1):
		var step: float = (S()[i].g - S()[i - 1].g) * dir
		var max_step: float = S()[i].d / RAMP + EPS
		worst = maxf(worst, step)
		if step < -EPS or step > max_step:
			ok = false
	return {"ok": ok, "worst_step": worst}

func all_in_band(a: int, b: int) -> bool:
	if a < 0 or b < a:
		return false
	for i in range(a, b + 1):
		if not in_band(S()[i].g):
			return false
	return true

# Indices of the strict local maxima of g in [a, b] (a > 0, b < size - 1). A tie with the next
# sample counts once, on the first of the pair (at 30 fps the peak at t = 0.25 s falls between
# two samples that are equal up to rounding).
func local_maxima(a: int, b: int) -> Array[int]:
	var peaks: Array[int] = []
	for i in range(maxi(a, 1), mini(b, S().size() - 2) + 1):
		if S()[i].g > S()[i - 1].g and S()[i].g >= S()[i + 1].g:
			peaks.append(i)
	return peaks

func min_max(a: int, b: int) -> Dictionary:
	var lo := INF
	var hi := -INF
	for i in range(a, b + 1):
		lo = minf(lo, S()[i].g)
		hi = maxf(hi, S()[i].g)
	return {"min": lo, "max": hi}

func run() -> void:
	sampler = Sampler.new()
	sampler.process_priority = 100
	root.add_child(sampler)

	# --- A2 / F4: the shader's interface, from the engine and from the source text ---
	var shader: Shader = load(SHADER_PATH)
	var uniforms: Array = shader.get_shader_uniform_list()
	var types := {}
	var raw: Array = []
	for u in uniforms:
		types[String(u.name)] = int(u.type)
		raw.append({"name": String(u.name), "type": int(u.type), "hint": int(u.hint), "hint_string": String(u.hint_string)})
	check("shader-uniforms", uniforms.size() == 2 and types.get("glow", -1) == TYPE_FLOAT and types.get("glow_color", -1) == TYPE_COLOR,
		{"uniforms": raw, "TYPE_FLOAT": TYPE_FLOAT, "TYPE_COLOR": TYPE_COLOR})
	var src: String = FileAccess.get_file_as_string(SHADER_PATH)
	var re_glow := RegEx.create_from_string("uniform\\s+float\\s+glow\\s*:\\s*hint_range\\(\\s*0\\.0\\s*,\\s*1\\.0\\s*\\)\\s*=\\s*0\\.0\\s*;")
	var re_color := RegEx.create_from_string("uniform\\s+vec4\\s+glow_color\\s*:\\s*source_color\\s*=\\s*vec4\\(\\s*0\\.6\\s*,\\s*0\\.85\\s*,\\s*1\\.0\\s*,\\s*1\\.0\\s*\\)\\s*;")
	check("shader-defaults", re_glow.search(src) != null and re_color.search(src) != null,
		{"glow_default_line": re_glow.search(src) != null, "glow_color_default_line": re_color.search(src) != null, "source_bytes": src.length()})
	var re_line := RegEx.create_from_string("COLOR\\.rgb\\s*=\\s*mix\\(\\s*COLOR\\.rgb\\s*,\\s*glow_color\\.rgb\\s*,\\s*glow\\s*\\)\\s*;")
	check("colour-line", re_line.search(src) != null, {"a2_colour_line_present": re_line.search(src) != null})
	var driver_param: String = load(DRIVER_PATH).PARAM
	check("driver-param-declared", types.has(driver_param), {"driver_writes": driver_param, "shader_declares": types.keys()})

	# --- A2 / F5 / R8: where the material sits ---
	await fresh()
	var mat: Material = game.player.sprite.material
	var mat_shader_path: String = mat.shader.resource_path if mat is ShaderMaterial and mat.shader else ""
	check("material-on-sprite", mat is ShaderMaterial and mat_shader_path == SHADER_PATH and game.player.material == null and game.player.art.material == null,
		{"sprite_material": str(mat), "shader": mat_shader_path, "player_material": str(game.player.material), "art_material": str(game.player.art.material)})

	# --- R1: nothing glows before W ---
	var pre_n := S().size()
	var pre_ok := pre_n >= 3
	for i in range(pre_n):
		if S()[i].g != 0.0 or S()[i].h:
			pre_ok = false
	check("glow-starts-zero", pre_ok, {"frames": pre_n, "last": S()[pre_n - 1] if pre_n > 0 else null})

	# --- R1, R3, R4, F1 (Revision 3): W through the game loop; ramp from 0 into the band ---
	# The brief says "into the band within 0.25 s". At the ramp rate 1/RAMP the band's low edge
	# (0.4) is reached in 0.4 × 0.25 = 0.1 s, asserted to one frame as well, so a slower ramp (F1)
	# is still caught on the way up now that 1.0 is no longer the target.
	var press_at := S().size()
	key(KEY_W, true)
	await steps(2)
	key(KEY_W, false)
	var guard := 0
	while guard < 200 and first_from(press_at, func(s): return in_band(s.g)) < 0:
		await steps(1)
		guard += 1
	var i_rise := first_from(press_at, func(s): return s.g > 0.0)
	var i0 := last_before(i_rise, func(s): return s.g == 0.0) if i_rise > 0 else -1
	var i1 := first_from(press_at, func(s): return in_band(s.g))
	var d: float = S()[i1].d if i1 >= 0 else 0.0
	var up_frames := i1 - i0
	var up_time := up_frames * d
	var up_expected := BAND_LO * RAMP
	var g_max := 0.0
	for s in S():
		g_max = maxf(g_max, s.g)
	check("ramp-up-time", i0 >= 0 and i1 > i0 and up_time <= RAMP + d + EPS and absf(up_time - up_expected) <= d + EPS and g_max <= BAND_HI + BAND_EPS and S()[i_rise].h,
		{"delta": d, "fps_from_delta": 1.0 / d if d > 0.0 else 0.0, "frames": up_frames, "seconds": up_time, "within": RAMP, "expected_at_ramp_rate": up_expected, "tolerance": d, "max_glow": g_max, "hosing_at_first_rise": S()[i_rise].h if i_rise >= 0 else null})
	var up := monotone(i0, i1, 1.0)
	check("ramp-up-monotonic", up.ok, {"from": i0, "to": i1, "worst_step": up.worst_step, "max_step": d / RAMP})

	# --- R5, F2: a second W during the glow changes nothing ---
	var ticks_before: int = game.water_ticks
	var ext_before: int = game.extinguish_ticks
	var near: bool = game.near_fire
	var retrig_at := S().size()
	key(KEY_W, true)
	await steps(2)
	key(KEY_W, false)
	await steps(1)
	check("retrigger-ignored", near and ext_before > 0 and game.water_ticks < ticks_before and game.sfx_counts.hose == 1 and all_in_band(retrig_at, S().size() - 1),
		{"near_fire": near, "water_ticks_before": ticks_before, "water_ticks_after": game.water_ticks, "hose_sounds": game.sfx_counts.hose, "samples_since": S().size() - retrig_at})

	# --- R6 (Revision 2, band per Revision 3): the game's pause during the hold ---
	# The game pause freezes water_ticks (the hold) but leaves player.hosing true and does not pause
	# the tree, so the driver, which reads only player.hosing, keeps breathing inside the band. The
	# check asserts the band; min/max over the paused frames are recorded so the log shows whether
	# the value moved. A value frozen outright needs a tree pause (R6), which this test does not do.
	game.set_paused(true)
	var pause_at := S().size()
	var ticks_paused: int = game.water_ticks
	await steps(10)
	var paused_mm := min_max(pause_at, S().size() - 1)
	check("pause-holds", game.state == Game.State.PAUSED and game.water_ticks == ticks_paused and S().size() - pause_at >= 10 and all_in_band(pause_at, S().size() - 1),
		{"state": game.state, "water_ticks": game.water_ticks, "frames_paused": S().size() - pause_at, "glow_min_while_paused": paused_mm.min, "glow_max_while_paused": paused_mm.max, "glow_moved_while_paused": paused_mm.max - paused_mm.min > BAND_EPS})
	game.set_paused(false)

	# --- R1/R3 hold (Revision 3): after the first 0.25 s every hosing sample is in [0.4, 0.8] ---
	guard = 0
	while guard < 2000 and (game.player.hosing or not zero(S().back().g)):
		await steps(1)
		guard += 1
	var i_h := first_from(press_at, func(s): return s.h)         # hosing began (t = 0)
	var j0 := last_before(S().size(), func(s): return s.h)        # last hosing sample
	var band_from := i_h + ceili(RAMP / d - EPS)                  # first sample at t >= 0.25 s
	var hold_mm := min_max(band_from, j0)
	check("hold-in-band", i_h >= 0 and j0 > band_from and all_in_band(band_from, j0),
		{"hosing_from": i_h, "band_from": band_from, "last_hosing": j0, "hold_frames": j0 - i_h + 1, "hold_seconds": (j0 - i_h + 1) * d, "min": hold_mm.min, "max": hold_mm.max, "band": [BAND_LO, BAND_HI], "band_eps": BAND_EPS})

	# --- the signal breathes: at least 4 local maxima in the hold, reaching both ends of the band ---
	var peaks := local_maxima(i_h + 1, j0 - 1)
	var peak_values: Array = []
	for p in peaks:
		peak_values.append(S()[p].g)
	check("hold-breathes", peaks.size() >= 4 and hold_mm.max >= BAND_HI - REACH_EPS and hold_mm.min <= BAND_LO + REACH_EPS,
		{"maxima": peaks.size(), "maxima_at": peaks, "maxima_values": peak_values, "min": hold_mm.min, "max": hold_mm.max, "reach_eps": REACH_EPS})

	# --- period 1.0 s, peak to peak, within one frame period at this frame rate ---
	var gaps_s: Array = []
	var period_ok := peaks.size() >= 2
	var worst_gap := 0.0
	for k in range(1, peaks.size()):
		var gap_s: float = (peaks[k] - peaks[k - 1]) * d
		gaps_s.append(gap_s)
		worst_gap = maxf(worst_gap, absf(gap_s - PERIOD))
		if absf(gap_s - PERIOD) > d + EPS:
			period_ok = false
	check("hold-period", period_ok, {"peak_to_peak_seconds": gaps_s, "expected": PERIOD, "tolerance": d, "worst_error": worst_gap})

	# --- R2, R3: the hold is the game's; the down-ramp starts the frame hosing ends ---
	# From a band value g the ramp at rate 1/RAMP takes g × 0.25 s (≤ 0.25 s), asserted to one frame.
	var j1 := first_from(j0 + 1, func(s): return zero(s.g)) if j0 >= 0 else -1
	var down_frames := j1 - j0
	var down_time := down_frames * d
	var g_at_end: float = S()[j0].g if j0 >= 0 else -1.0
	var down_expected := g_at_end * RAMP
	var hold_ok: bool = j0 >= 0 and j0 + 1 < S().size() and in_band(g_at_end) and S()[j0].h and not S()[j0 + 1].h
	var down := monotone(j0, j1, -1.0)
	check("hold-is-game-time", hold_ok and j1 > j0 and absf(down_time - down_expected) <= d + EPS and down_time <= RAMP + d + EPS and zero(S().back().g) and down.ok,
		{"hold_frames": j0 - i_h + 1, "hold_seconds": (j0 - i_h + 1) * d, "glow_at_last_hosing": g_at_end, "hosing_at_last": S()[j0].h, "hosing_next_frame": S()[j0 + 1].h, "down_frames": down_frames, "down_seconds": down_time, "expected": down_expected, "tolerance": d, "monotone": down.ok, "worst_step": down.worst_step, "last": S().back().g, "water_ticks": game.water_ticks})

	# --- R7: R mid-ramp; glow descends from where it is, never jumps ---
	await fresh()
	key(KEY_W, true)
	var r_at := -1
	guard = 0
	while guard < 100 and r_at < 0:
		await steps(1)
		guard += 1
		var g: float = S().back().g
		if g > 0.3 and g < 0.7:
			key(KEY_R, true)
			r_at = S().size() - 1   # the sample on screen when R was posted
	await steps(2)
	key(KEY_R, false)
	key(KEY_W, false)
	guard = 0
	while guard < 100 and not zero(S().back().g):
		await steps(1)
		guard += 1
	var peak_idx := r_at
	for i in range(r_at, S().size()):
		if S()[i].g > S()[peak_idx].g:
			peak_idx = i
	var peak: float = S()[peak_idx].g if r_at >= 0 else -1.0
	var k1 := first_from(peak_idx + 1, func(s): return zero(s.g)) if r_at >= 0 else -1
	var dn := monotone(peak_idx, k1, -1.0)
	var restarted: bool = game.state == Game.State.PLAYING and game.water_ticks == 0 and game.player.position.distance_to(Vector2(64, 320)) < 1.0
	check("restart-mid-ramp", r_at >= 0 and peak <= BAND_HI + BAND_EPS and peak > 0.3 and peak_idx - r_at <= 2 and k1 > peak_idx and dn.ok and (k1 - peak_idx) * d <= RAMP + d + EPS and restarted,
		{"glow_at_R": S()[r_at].g if r_at >= 0 else null, "peak": peak, "frames_until_descent": peak_idx - r_at, "down_frames": k1 - peak_idx, "down_seconds": (k1 - peak_idx) * d, "monotone": dn.ok, "worst_step": dn.worst_step, "restarted": restarted, "state": game.state, "water_ticks": game.water_ticks})

	print("HOSE GLOW TESTS: %d checks / %d failures (process delta %.6f s)" % [results.size(), failures, d])
	game.queue_free()
	await process_frame
	quit(1 if failures else 0)
